rites.name: Xaeseth
rites.text: Xaeseth is the concept of the first sounding of Grimozhun's roots, a resonance held in the Singing that gathers the scattered substance of Ki into lasting form. During the Age of Sundering its tone was said to tear apart the old bonds that held landfall together, leaving the world to settle along new seams.

rites.name: Venilae
rites.text: Venilae is a concept of Grimozhun that hums through the Singing, the undated sounding in which the first roots of the world condense into shape. Its voice was said to split the old bonds during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the ancient continents apart. Sages still debate whether it rings the world into being or merely announces that it has already begun.

rites.name: Nintia
rites.text: A discipline of breath that lets a trained person channel a radiant inner current through the body. It is a sunlight-like force that stands opposed to the draining power of undead creatures.

rites.name: Tonernor
rites.text: A hereditary sacred power passed down within one family line, awakened by living near a cursed desert landmark. It lets its wielder command vast quantities of sand and shape the surrounding wasteland.

rites.name: Veosor
rites.text: A power that rises from a person's repeated bodily and heartfelt suffering. It is harder to command than other gifts and tends to act against whatever keeps causing the bearer pain.

rites.name: Tinostium
rites.text: A dark inner fire that seizes a person when they are desperate for a cherished aim. It sweeps away conscience and grants fearless ruthlessness, though those who surrender to it often meet a grim fate later.

rites.name: Amallor
rites.text: A chalk-drawing power that marks shapes upon the ground. Anyone who breaks its set rules falls into hidden pits laid beneath the marked lines.

rites.name: Orirnus
rites.text: A close-range spirit-power bound to a traveler who roams the wide plains. It stands alongside its wielder in the midst of a long journey.

rites.name: Telinteoria
rites.text: A fiery spirit-power that a wandering sorcerer calls forth from within himself. It fights alongside its wielder in close quarters, bound to the one who awakened it.

rites.name: Sirnium
rites.text: A bearer can direct a swarm of nearby insects by commanding where they should strike. The same power can stiffen the swarm's bodies into unseen, deadly projectiles.

rites.name: Ciantastia
rites.text: A rapid sequence of close-range blows delivered at great speed, often accompanied by a loud roar from the striker. It is one of the most recognizable combat techniques in the setting and appears in many later depictions.

rites.name: Telestanum
rites.text: A close-range power that strikes with raw fists and whips up scorching gales that burn opponents. It awakens late in its bearer's life through a copied relic and is used only once, in a decisive clash.

rites.name: Ameontor
rites.text: Ameontor is the concept of the Walled Age in Grimozhun, the idea that a boundary held for centuries becomes sacred in itself. Its orders keep the old walls standing, and its churches teach that the first crossing of any barrier is the moment a people becomes real. It is felt most strongly where a wall has never been breached.

rites.name: Crudardath
rites.text: Crudardath is the concept of the wall itself as Grimozhun understood it in the Walled Age, a principle that held cities apart from the wild and was kept by oaths, orders and the churches that tended the stone. Its first crossings, when a sworn gate was opened from within, are remembered as the moment the principle was first tested.

rites.name: Teloniasor
rites.text: A mutated inner force that a bearer's spirit takes on after being struck by a sharp relic during a final clash. It turns the original power into something stranger, with a fixed, unchanging purpose.

rites.name: Amerum
rites.text: A recorded chant tied to a fiery spirit-guardian of a wandering mage. It is sung by a single voice and serves as the signature melody for that guardian.

rites.name: Amania
rites.text: A recorded song of pursuit, composed and sung by a small band of four performers. It serves as a second musical opening for a long serialized story, and an English rendering appears on one of the group's later albums.

rites.name: Volisum
rites.text: A bearer can cast off their outer layer like a wrapping and emerge renewed. The gift belongs to one named wanderer whose tale appears in a novel of the realm.

rites.name: Sontes
rites.text: A hidden power wielded by a wandering figure whose origin remains unclear. Scholars cannot tell whether this gift comes from a bound spirit or from a distant, otherworldly source.

rites.name: Mariales
rites.text: A spirit-like power that a wanderer carries as a companion, sometimes called by a nickname. It is tied to a single hidden bearer who draws it forth.

rites.name: Rosteonia
rites.text: A bonded spirit-presence that dwells beside a single wielder and manifests as a companion. It shapes the wielder's strength in close bonds with another.

rites.name: Teostes
rites.text: A bound spinning force drawn from rolling metal spheres thrown in a sealed manner that can slip past barriers between realms. Anyone who trains in the spin art is said to be able to call it forth, provided they meet its demanding conditions.

rites.name: Soleornes
rites.text: A rare inner gift lets its bearer dissolve wholly into a surrounding element or landscape, becoming part of that setting itself. It is recorded in a single written account of a wanderer's travels.

rites.name: Teorallum
rites.text: A lingering affliction that clings to a bearer's mind and is wielded by a woman who dreads painted jesters. It was born from an old stalking by a murderer who left her haunted.

rites.name: Sistium
rites.text: A bearer's gift that lets them change how swiftly the projectiles they launch travel. It is a pure power, owned by one individual, which quickens or slows shots at will.

rites.name: Maleoranum
rites.text: A bound power that spins taut threads which coil unbidden around a target's limbs and sink into the skin. The threads cut deeper the more the bound one struggles.

rites.name: Nolor
rites.text: A forbidden word that no published work may print drifts into the mind of a rival storyteller. His fixation on it grows until his grip on reason frays, showing that some words are banned for good reason.

rites.name: Rarnia
rites.text: A guardian form awakens after a sacred relic strikes its bearer, shielding the relic and reshaping the minds of companions so that their spirits swap vessels.

rites.name: Ventor
rites.text: A bird's inner power awakened after it swallowed a fragment of a sealed arrow. It guards a chosen zone by wiping away the aims of any being who steps inside.

rites.name: Siarnanum
rites.text: A gentle fern-like spirit-force that wakes in a bearer after a dark tyrant stirs. Its kindness slips beyond its keeper's control and slowly wears the bearer down.

rites.name: Seosonor
rites.text: A rare inborn talent lets a storyteller flawlessly copy, seize, and steer other people's voices by taking in their spit or tongue. She draws on it to give her written tales lifelike speech.

rites.name: Teollia
rites.text: A sleeping creature's spirit slips out of its body at night and takes control of others' bodies, moving them like sleepwalkers. It is awakened when a fragment of a mystic arrow is swallowed.

rites.name: Nirarnes
rites.text: A thinking spirit-force that bends the order of simultaneous moves in a clash, so its bearer always lands the first blow. It is aware and acts on its own judgment.

rites.name: Teleostilum
rites.text: A bodily discipline that lets its wielder govern each muscle with uncanny precision. The practitioner can tighten fibers in ways no ordinary body allows.

rites.name: Krairnak
rites.text: Krairnak is a concept-born presence in Grimozhun's Ki realm, sealed behind a door that exists only when no one is looking for it. Its influence is felt as small coincidences that steer an entire settlement toward outcomes it never chose.

rites.name: Thuktok
rites.text: Thuktok is a breath-cycled discipline in Grimozhun's Ki realm that gathers a warm, radiant life-current and drives it through flesh, blade, or still water. Its practitioners find that the current scorches anything animated by unnatural hunger, since the light mimics the sun those beings cannot survive. Adepts also learn quick healing, swift footwork, and a sight that reads the currents around them.

rites.name: Grakturn
rites.text: Grakturn is a discipline of the ember-soul, in which a practitioner's inner flame coalesces into a veiled familiar called a wick-shade, visible only to those who share its binding. Each shade carries one singular faculty, rated across six measures of ember, quickness, reach, toughness, exactness, and growth.

rites.name: Grimagozhar
rites.text: Grimagozhar is a hollow state of being imposed on a mortal by a cold, toothed relic of the Ki realm, granting uncanny strength, quickened reflexes, and flesh that knits itself back together. Its bearers gain a signature technique of their own design, yet every mending is paid for with a dread weakness to the rising light and to the gold-threaded breath of the sun-faithful.

rites.name: Groukak
rites.text: Groukak is a pale, thread-like spore-worm that its keepers seed into a living host through a single hair or a fresh wound. Once rooted along the spine it reknits the nervous system so the seeder can steer the body from afar, and when the host dies it can animate the corpse instead. The Ki-cult of Grimozhun guards its cultivation, having learned that a single grown colony can bind a whole district's servants at once.

rites.name: Gogun
rites.text: Gogun is the sealed apex of an ancient line of stone-skinned climbers who learned to drink the light of a dying sun through a crimson heartstone buried beneath the Ki highlands. Its flesh reshapes itself with each new threat, hardening against any assault that has already been survived once. Scholars of the E6 era believe it was never meant to wake.

rites.name: Vorathoth
rites.text: Vorathoth is a cinder-hued mantle that awakens within a bonded Ki-spirit only when its wielder is wounded twice by the same ember-bolt, reshaping the spirit into a sovereign form that rewrites the rules of the fire it commands. Its second form can unmake the flow of time over a stretch of ash-plains, bending cause and consequence until the wind itself runs backward.

rites.name: Karuzhoktar
rites.text: Karuzhoktar is a spinning discipline of the Ki realm, taught in the wandering cloisters of Grimozhun during the sixth era, in which practitioners impart controlled whirl to coins, shot, and marbles. A spun object can bend its path around obstacles, slice through soft matter, or throw off the rhythm of a body's own turning currents. Its masters use it equally to wound and to mend.

rites.name: Gorkairnoth
rites.text: Gorkairnoth is a rare rotational discipline practiced in the sunken cloisters of Ki, where adepts whirl hollow ironwood drums until the air itself begins to coil. Its finest exponents are said to hurl a spinning lattice of compressed dusk that can tear the marrow from stone, though few chronicles agree on how it is taught.

rites.name: Koktaiggun
rites.text: Koktaiggun is a gravity-tuned concept-weapon grown in the sealed vaults of Grimozhun, an infant-shaped lattice that bends local mass into shifting wells. Its presence is said to slow the ticking of nearby clocks and fold distant horizons toward a single point. It is held in suspension because any sustained use tears open the seams of the realm it stands within.

rites.name: Thutharnak
rites.text: Thutharnak is a glassy, hollow-boned mechanism-spirit of the Ki realm in Grimozhun, built to hoard the dormant sparks left behind by fallen engines. When it devours a sealed spark it grows a new faculty, which the caravan-scribes call its harvests. Its harvests are tallied in an old ledger that nobody living can fully read.

rites.name: Drazhouktak
rites.text: Drazhouktak is the sorting grammar that Ki-realm scholars of Grimozhun use to file every mind-born power into a handful of tidy kinds: near-reach bodies, far-reach bodies, wills that act without their bearer, anchors fused to a single place, and swarms of tiny cooperating shards. Its categories are loose enough to describe nearly any power, and every new discovery is taken as proof that the scheme needs one more column.

rites.name: Valenor Telosium
rites.text: A cosmic blessing flows through a chosen bearer and lets an ally reach a higher form. Its power over ill fortune is so vast that only a force of equal magnitude can resist it.
